The arsenal site lies off Route 673 northwest of its junction with VA 147.
evidence.quote: It is located near Midlothian, Virginia, off State Route 673 northwest of its junction with VA 147.

evidence.claim: A gristmill established in the 1730s helped form the community at Fine Creek’s lower falls.
evidence.quote: the community of Fine Creek Mills developed as early as the 1730s when a gristmill was established along the creek.

evidence.claim: A road beside the creek led to the James River ferry at Lee’s Landing, connecting the mills to the river and railroad to Richmond.
evidence.quote: With a road along Fine Creek leading to the ferry across the James River at Lee's Landing, Fine Creek Mills served as an important link to the James River and the railroad to Richmond.

evidence.claim: The community remained a commercial center into the mid-20th century, with a school, store and post office.
evidence.quote: The community continued to flourish as a commercial center for the area into the mid 20th century with a school, post office and store also located there.

evidence.claim: The historic district includes mill ruins, the Fine Creek Manor site and a miller’s house dating from the mid-18th century.
evidence.quote: The property included in the district consists of the Fine Creek Mill Ruins, the Fine Creek Manor Site (Peter Jefferson Home Site), and the Miller's House, dating from the mid-18th century

evidence.claim: An early-20th-century school, store and gatehouse associated with cheese production also belong to the district, alongside the older milling remains.
evidence.quote: as well as the Gatehouse/Cheese Factory, the Fine Creek School, the Store and the Chase-Harris House, all of which date to the early 20th century.

evidence.claim: The chapel’s pointed windows and three-sided entrance belong to an 1895 church, the fourth building to serve King William Parish.
evidence.quote: A simple wood-frame country church in a modified Gothic Revival style, the chapel was erected in 1895 as Manakin Church, the fourth such building to serve King William Parish

evidence.claim: The chapel’s pointed windows and three-sided entrance
evidence.quote: The building is set off by its distinctive three-sided narthex and pointed side windows.

evidence.claim: Older materials complicate that date. In 1985, architectural historians Calder Loth and Edward Chappell confirmed that the building reused parts of earlier structures.
evidence.quote: An architectural examination of the chapel conducted in September 1985 by Calder Loth, senior architectural historian of the Virginia Division of Historic Landmarks, and Edward Chappell director of architectural research of the Colonial Williamsburg Foundation, confirmed the tradition that the chapel is partly constructed of materials salvaged from earlier buildings.

evidence.claim: Loth raised the possibility that a charred beam came from the second Manakin church, erected circa 1710 and destroyed by fire about 1729. That identification remains a theory, not an established construction date for the chapel.
evidence.quote: A charred 4'x 9" section removed from the front end and displayed in the nave, has raised the possibility that the beam is a fragment of the second Manakin Church, erected ca. 1710 and destroyed by fire about 1729.

evidence.claim: The building moved in 1954 and again in 1985, when it reached land owned by the society preserving it.
evidence.quote: The chapel was moved approximately 200 feet to the south in 1954 to make way for the present church. In 1985 it was moved to its present location

evidence.claim: when it reached land owned by the society preserving it.
evidence.quote: in order to have the chapel on property owned by the Society of the Founders of Manakin

evidence.claim: Old Gun Road’s name comes from two neighboring establishments: Bellona Foundry and Bellona Arsenal.
evidence.quote: The arsenal and foundry are the namesake of "Old Gun Road" in the Robious area of Chesterfield County.

evidence.claim: The foundry began in 1810; the Army erected the arsenal in 1816 and began storing the foundry’s cannon there the next year.
evidence.quote: Maj. Clarke arranged for the location of a federal arsenal immediately to the west of Bellona Foundry. The Army erected Bellona Arsenal in 1816. It began storing cannon from the Foundry in 1817.

evidence.claim: The foundry began in 1810
evidence.quote: established the Bellona Foundry on the south shore of the James River, 14 miles west of Richmond, Virginia, in 1810.

evidence.claim: After the War Department declared the arsenal surplus in 1837, several buildings became a silkworm farm. During the Civil War, the complex manufactured Confederate armaments.
evidence.quote: In 1837 the War Department declared disused Bellona Arsenal surplus.  Thomas Randolph and a partner leased several buildings for a silkworm farm.

evidence.claim: During the Civil War, the complex manufactured Confederate armaments.
evidence.quote: Bellona Arsenal and the somewhat larger Tredegar Iron Works manufactured cannons and similar armaments for the Confederate military.

evidence.claim: Later demolition removed much of the quadrangle.
evidence.quote: The owners tore down the barracks, quarters for officers, and one workshop in 1872; only three workshops of the original eight quadrangle buildings (and the powder magazine) survived

evidence.claim: In 1942, C. Merle Luck bought the surviving buildings and began renovations, later converting them into residences.
evidence.quote: in 1942, Mr. C. Merle Luck purchased the surviving buildings and began to renovate them.  He later converted them into residences.

evidence.claim: Later demolition removed much of the quadrangle. The powder magazine survives without its roof.
evidence.quote: The powder magazine has survived to the present but has no roof.
